title: In-class DKA: Caleb Mercer (36 h, checkpoints every 4 hours)
diagnosis: Moderate-to-severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 7.18, bicarbonate 8, beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.4, anion gap 28) in type 1 diabetes after stopping basal insulin during a viral illness
desc: Mon 01/11 0700 to Tue 01/12 1900 in ten 4-hour checkpoints (in class; bedside monitor MRN SIM-40601). A 28-year-old with type 1 diabetes stopped his long-acting insulin for 2 nights during a flu-like illness and arrives from the ED on fixed-rate insulin. Adult DKA protocol with a dextrose line and peripheral potassium riders, droplet precautions, potassium and glucose changes on treatment, IV site care, the transition to subcutaneous insulin, sick-day teaching and discharge planning. Vital signs and bedside glucoses after 0700 come from the monitor and the instructor.
